text: The circle \(C\) has equation \(x^2+y^2-4x+6y-12=0\). Find the centre and radius of \(C\).
Points \(A(1,1)\), \(B(5,3)\) and \(C(3,7)\). Which working correctly shows that angle \(ABC=90^\circ\)?
working: \(m_{AB}=\frac{3-1}{5-1}=\frac12\), \(m_{BC}=\frac{7-3}{3-5}=-2\). Product \(=-1\), so \(AB\perp BC\). (Equal lengths alone do not prove a right angle.)

text: Points \(A(1,1)\), \(B(5,3)\) and \(C(3,7)\). Angle \(ABC=90^\circ\). Find the equation of the circle through \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\).
working: Right angle at \(B\) \(\Rightarrow AC\) is a diameter. Centre = midpoint of \(AC=(2,4)\); \(r^2=\frac{(3-1)^2+(7-1)^2}{4}=10\).

The circle \((x-3)^2+(y+1)^2=25\) and the line \(l: y=x+1\). Find the coordinates of the points where \(l\) meets the circle.
The circle \((x-3)^2+(y+1)^2=25\) and the line \(l: y=x+1\). \(l\) meets the circle at \((3,4)\) and \((-2,-1)\). Find the length of the chord.
A circle touches the \(x\)-axis at \((4,0)\) and passes through \((0,2)\). Find the radius of the circle.
working: Touching the \(x\)-axis at \((4,0)\) \(\Rightarrow\) centre \((4,r)\). Then \(4^2+(2-r)^2=r^2 \Rightarrow 20-4r=0 \Rightarrow r=5\).

text: A circle touches the \(x\)-axis at \((4,0)\) and passes through \((0,2)\). Its radius is \(5\). Write down its equation.

The line \(l_1\) is \(3x+y=7\). The line \(l_2\) passes through \(P(2,3)\) and is perpendicular to \(l_1\). \(l_2\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(A\) and the \(y\)-axis at \(B\). \(O\) is the origin. Find the equation of \(l_2\).
working: Gradient of \(l_1\) is \(-3\), so gradient of \(l_2\) is \(\frac13\): \(y-3=\frac13(x-2) \Rightarrow x-3y+7=0\).
